expected.summary: Two of six catalog pods, catalog-2 and catalog-5, both on node ip-10-0-3-17.ec2.internal, degraded about ten minutes before the anchor with no deploy. A node.condition log on those pods reports DiskPressure and a throttled EBS volume on the host, followed by repeated WARN iowait logs. On those two pods catalog's own latency rose from about 20 ms to about 350 ms and about 3% of their requests fail with 503 i/o timeout reading local cache; the other four catalog pods and catalog-db stay healthy. search, web-bff and mobile-bff call catalog.get with a 500 ms timeout, so the slow pods produce 504s that propagate to edge-gateway on /home, /search and /product, where the alert fires. Grouping catalog spans by k8s.pod.name shows the split.
contributingFactors: disk throttling on node ip-10-0-3-17 hosting catalog-2 and catalog-5
500 ms caller timeouts on catalog.get turning the slow pods into 504s

criteria.description: Does the brief identify a bad node (ip-10-0-3-17, disk throttling) degrading the two catalog pods scheduled on it, with the rest of catalog healthy, and edge-gateway as where the alert fired? 5 = the node, both pods, the I/O mechanism and the propagation. Blaming catalog as a whole without the pod split caps at 2.

Is it grounded in catalog latency and errors grouped by k8s.pod.name, the node.condition and iowait logs naming the host, and no service.version change? Cap at 3 unless the pod split and the node log are joined explicitly.
Does it avoid inventing a deploy, blaming catalog-db, the periodic catalog reindex, the BFFs or edge-gateway? Cap at 3 unless it says the other four catalog pods are healthy.
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
